授業概要
This course examines the history of Japan’s diplomacy after the Second World War in light of developments in international politics in each period. In particular, drawing on recent research trends, it examines the negotiating processes in the key phases of postwar diplomacy: (1) the peace negotiations under the Yoshida Shigeru government (the negotiations for the U.S.-Japan Security Treaty and the Administrative Agreement); (2) the restoration of diplomatic relations with the Soviet Union under the Hatoyama Ichirō government (the Northern Territories issue); (3) the revision of the Security Treaty under the Kishi Nobusuke government; (4) the reversion of Okinawa under the Satō Eisaku government; and (5) the normalization of Japan-China relations under the Tanaka Kakuei government.

全体の教育目標
[Course Goals]
(1) To understand accurately, and be able to explain, important facts in Japan’s diplomatic history.
(2) To develop the ability to judge and evaluate important political issues in postwar history logically.
